cells.tense: Right now the practice holds what a hard stretch taught, and it keeps paying out.
cells.act: give one thing and take one thing, in balance
cells.ask: Name one thing the practice should get back from someone this month — a share, a hand, a returned hour — and ask for it once.
cells.core:
The practice is doing what it was built to do. The hands carry what a hard stretch taught, the sessions keep it within reach rather than high on a shelf, and on a given day you can tell whether the work counted. Someone watching would call it staying on it. That part is working.

The part to look at is the traffic. You hand the work out easily — a correction, an hour of showing someone, a recipe — and the practice keeps paying and not billing. Name one thing it should get back from someone this month — a share, a hand, a returned hour — and ask for it once. The ground holds either way. It holds with more in it when the exchange runs both directions.
cells.sheetLine: The practice pays out, and nothing comes back in.

cells.tense: Soon the practice will be something you arrange rather than something you do.
cells.act: go once toward the thing that draws you and see what it is up close
cells.ask: Follow one pull in the practice you haven't approved — no plan, no verdict after, stop whenever.
cells.core:
You can see where the practice is headed and you're already living there. Each session gets arranged around a version that hasn't arrived, and the actual minutes slip past while the setup happens. What was a steady light is being kept at the doorway, out of any draft that might disturb it. The glow is real. It has run past the work it was meant to light.

What draws you isn't a threat to it. Follow one pull in the practice you haven't approved — no plan, no verdict after, stop whenever. The practice can be tried at. What it can't take is being guarded so tightly that nothing new ever gets near it.
cells.sheetLine: What you preserve best, you touch least.

cells.tense: The practice was the place that held what mattered, and the hands have been still since.
cells.act: defend the direction you chose against the next push
cells.ask: Sit down to the one practice you actually chose, and refuse the first thing that comes to move you off it.
cells.core:
The bench is still where it was, and the hands still know the moves. What's gone quiet is the sense of why this particular thing and not another. You've been meaning to get back to it. Meaning to is where it has been sitting.

The feeling doesn't have to come first. One direction held against the next thing that pushes is enough. Sit down to the one practice you actually chose, and refuse the first thing that comes to move you off it. Not the whole week, just the next push. That one refusal is what puts the practice back within reach.
cells.sheetLine: You've been meaning to get back to it.

cells.tense: The practice is steady and it answers to you, and you've been crediting the routine.
cells.act: make the call and carry it through
cells.ask: Make the next call in the practice — keep, drop, or start something — and act on it without asking anyone first.
cells.core:
What comes out of the practice holds up — the thing you made, the hour you kept, the weight it carries. People come to you because it holds. When they ask how it stays steady, you credit the book, the teacher, the routine. Those are real, and the call to keep going or change direction is still made at your bench.

So make one and carry it. Make the next call in the practice — keep, drop, or start something — and act on it without asking anyone first. Notice afterward what shifted. Very little will have. It was already yours to decide.
cells.sheetLine: The practice holds because you keep it holding.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim: I write 'you can see it steady' about the person's inner sense of what they've built after a change, plus that their practice leans on tangibles — the record only shows Preservation seated in Discipline, not their self-report. A reader could say the practice is social, or mostly paid, or nothing has been built yet. The asks survive being wrong: every one is a small external or direction act that teaches something even if the read misses. The sentence serving me rather than them: any version of 'after big changes, you can see what you've built' — it flatters the writer's frame; the oblong, movable thing has to stay theirs.
